history.heading: Ancient civilisations
paragraphs: Pakistan's territory includes the heartland of the Indus Valley Civilisation, one of the world's earliest urban cultures, with cities such as Mohenjo-daro and Harappa (around 2600–1900 BCE). Mehrgarh is one of the oldest farming settlements in South Asia.

The region was later part of the Persian Achaemenid Empire, conquered by Alexander the Great, and home to the Gandhara civilisation, a centre of Buddhist art and learning, with the university at Taxila.

history.heading: Islam and the Mughals
paragraphs: Arab forces brought Islam to Sindh in 711. Turkic and Afghan dynasties later ruled the region, which became central to the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughal Empire; Lahore was an important Mughal capital, with the Badshahi Mosque and Shalimar Gardens. The Sikh Empire of Ranjit Singh ruled Punjab in the early 19th century before British conquest.

history.heading: Creation of Pakistan
paragraphs: Under British rule, Muslim political leaders, led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah and inspired by the poet-philosopher Muhammad Iqbal, demanded a separate homeland for India's Muslims. Pakistan was created on 14 August 1947 with the partition of British India, which caused mass migration and violence. Pakistan consisted of two parts, West and East Pakistan, separated by India.
East Pakistan broke away after a brutal war in 1971 and became Bangladesh. Pakistan has fought several wars with India, mainly over Kashmir, and both countries tested nuclear weapons in 1998.

history.heading: Military and civilian rule
paragraphs: Pakistan has alternated between civilian governments and military rule, under generals Ayub Khan, Zia-ul-Haq and Pervez Musharraf. Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was executed in 1979, and his daughter Benazir Bhutto, the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority democracy, was assassinated in 2007.

Pakistan suffered heavily from terrorism linked to the Afghan wars. Former cricket star Imran Khan was prime minister from 2018 until his removal in 2022 and later imprisonment. In May 2025 a brief military conflict with India followed a terrorist attack in Kashmir.

culture.heading: Languages and faith
paragraphs: Urdu is the national language and English is official; Punjabi, Pashto, Sindhi, Saraiki and Balochi are widely spoken. About 96 percent of Pakistanis are Muslim, mostly Sunni, with a Shia minority, and there are Christian, Hindu and Ahmadi minorities who face discrimination.
Sufi traditions are important, with qawwali devotional music made famous worldwide by Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan. Poets such as Iqbal and Faiz Ahmed Faiz are revered.

culture.heading: Food and sport
paragraphs: Pakistani cuisine includes biryani, nihari, karahi, kebabs and flatbreads, with strong regional variations. Cricket is a national passion; Pakistan won the Cricket World Cup in 1992 under Imran Khan. Pakistan is also known for its mountains, including K2, the world's second-highest peak.

politics.heading: Federal parliamentary republic
paragraphs: Pakistan is a federal parliamentary republic with four provinces: Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, plus federally administered territories. The prime minister leads the government. The military remains the most powerful institution, with great influence over politics and foreign policy; a 2025 constitutional amendment further strengthened the army chief's role.

Major issues include tensions with India over Kashmir, militancy in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, strained relations with Afghanistan's Taliban government, and political polarisation around Imran Khan.

economy.heading: Economic structure
paragraphs: Pakistan has a large, mainly agricultural and textile-based economy. It is a major exporter of cotton textiles, clothing and rice. Remittances from Pakistanis in the Gulf and Britain are vital. The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor has financed infrastructure and energy projects.

Pakistan has faced repeated balance-of-payments crises and IMF programmes, high inflation, low tax collection and energy shortages. Devastating floods in 2022 affected a third of the country. The currency is the Pakistani rupee.
